newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau governor hails Nobel prize for Timor pair.
newsitem.headline: Macau governor hails Nobel prize for Timor pair.

text.p: The governor of Portuguese-run Macau on Friday hailed the award of the Nobel Peace Prize to East Timor's Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo and resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta.
General Vasco Rocha Vieira told reporters he was "very satisfied" with the Nobel Committee's decision.

East Timor was a Portuguese colony for four centuries. Indonesia invaded in December 1975 and annexed it the following year. That act has not been recognised by the United Nations, which still regards Lisbon as the administering power.

The administration of Macau, a tiny territory on the south China coast that Lisbon is handing back to Beijing on December 20, 1999, has supported incoming East Timorese refugees since Vieira became governor in 1991.
Belo taught at a school in Macau in the mid-1970s, and visited the local Catholic diocese and East Timorese community in May. Ramos-Horta is also a frequent visitor to Macau.
Vieira said he would send messages "of solidarity and great joy" to the prize winners.

He added the award of the prize to Belo and Ramos-Horta represented the international community's recognition that a solution was still needed to the question of whether East Timorese should have the right to self determination.
"I hope that the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize may decisively contribute to find a fair solution," he said.
"The East Timor issue must have a solution based on international law."
